title: Why low rumbles travel farther than high squeaks
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why can I hear the bass from a party far away?
Why do high sounds fade faster?

explain.say: Hear music from far away and you mostly hear the thumping bass. The high notes have faded on the way.

draw.text: Why low rumbles travel farther than high squeaks

explain.say: As sound travels, the air soaks up some of its energy, turning it into a tiny bit of heat. Air absorbs high-pitched sounds far more than low ones, roughly in step with the pitch squared.
Low sounds also have long waves, often metres long, that bend around trees, buildings and hills. Short high-pitched waves are blocked or reflected more easily.
So low rumbles from elephants, foghorns and thunder carry for kilometres, while a bat's squeak fades within a few metres. That is why foghorns and ship horns are built to sound deep.

faq.q: Why do high sounds fade faster?
faq.a: Air absorbs the energy of high-pitched sound much more quickly than low-pitched sound. High notes also get blocked more easily by obstacles, so they die away over shorter distances.
asks: Why do high notes not travel far?
Why does a whistle fade quickly?

faq.q: Why can I hear the bass from a party far away?
faq.a: Bass notes are low-pitched, so the air absorbs them very little and their long waves bend around buildings. The high notes fade on the way, leaving only the thump.
asks: Why do I only hear the beat of distant music?
Why does bass go through walls?

faq.a: Low notes carry much farther through air and fog than high notes, so a deep foghorn can warn ships many kilometres away.
asks: Why do ship horns sound deep?

faq.q: Why do long waves bend around obstacles?
faq.a: Waves bend around things that are similar in size to their wavelength or smaller. Low sounds can have waves several metres long, so they flow around trees and houses.
asks: Why can I hear round corners?

faq.q: Do low and high sounds travel at different speeds?
faq.a: No. In air, all pitches travel at about the same speed, 343 metres per second. The difference is in how quickly they lose energy, not how fast they go.

facts: Air absorbs sound more strongly at higher frequencies, roughly in proportion to the square of the frequency over much of the audible range.
In air, sounds of all pitches travel at about the same speed.

quiz.say: From far across town you can only hear the boom of a band's bass drum. Why?
quiz.show: Only the bass reaches you because…

options.show: Air absorbs high notes more, and low waves bend around buildings
options.say: Air absorbs high notes more, and low waves bend around buildings

quiz.why: High-pitched sound loses energy quickly in air and is blocked easily, while long low waves fade slowly and bend round obstacles.

wrong.0: All pitches travel at the same speed in air.
wrong.2: Up close you would hear the other instruments too.
